newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude aims for $20.54 range top.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude aims for $20.54 range top.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+NYMEX June crude is approaching the top of the old range again and it needs to break convincingly over the April high at $20.54 to move into new territory.
+Gasoline and heating oil are also in a similar position although may have a little more work to do to break out.
NYMEX crude oil futures are facing nearby resistance at the old range high of $20.54 which, if convincingly conquered, would signal a move into new and higher territory, technical analysts said.
June crude oil finished the day a robust 72 cents a barrel firmer on Thursday at $20.34, while June heating oil gained 1.30 cents to 53.08 and unleaded gasoline climbed 2.19 cents a gallon to 62.50.
"In the shorter term the range rules until $20.54 gives way," said Bob MacMinn at MPAS in Toronto.
"If we settle above there that lifts a really big load off the market...there are a lot of stops above there."
"If that happens there is the right open interest for us to see some fairly dynamic short covering."
One Washington-based chart analyst saw the same level. "The key is $20.54," she said.
"If we break through that level then we move to new highs. And it looks like it might do it," she said. "My daily charts are all decisively up on crude."
"If that fails, though, we are looking at a selloff back to the bottom of the old range, around $19.00-$19.50."
MacMinn said gasoline was also looking optimistic.
He said a bullish engulfing pattern on the ACCESS-included chart on May 7 had set the stage for Thursday's upwards move and was still providing bullish sentiment.
Both chartists saw resistance at the recent range top at 63.40 cents a gallon, which lay next to the 200-day moving average at 63.54.
"That number (63.40) is gasoline's equivalent of $20.54 on the crude," MacMinn said.
Heating oil faces resistance at the deep gap on the front-month continuation chart between 55.40 and 57.50.
"The stochastics have turned sharply to the up side and I expect that gap to get filled over the next week or two," he said.
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
